observations: A large central figure sits with limbs extended outward, outlined in layered black and blue lines over a warm field of red, ochre, and olive.
A white rectangular outline near the upper center floats unattached to any figure, with a bright white zigzag line descending from it toward the lower right.
At least four smaller tooth-baring mouths appear at the corners and edges—upper left, lower left, upper right—each rendered in tight black lines with white fill.
reading: The image crowds its space with figures and fragments: a seated central form, smaller shapes at the bottom, and bared teeth recurring at the margins. Blue line work runs across warm reds and ochres, while the floating white rectangle holds open a gap in the density. The repeated mouth motif reads as agitation or warning, though the layering keeps any single reading unstable.
contextAngle: Within the owned nnotb subset, this work sits between title neighbors nnxyz nnotb #18 and nnxyz nnotb #20. Where #18 isolates a single figure on a plain ground and #20 dissolves into soft repeated organic forms, #19 packs multiple figures and recurring mouth fragments into a dense warm-field composition.

connections.reason: Both works use white line to define a central figure against a colored ground, but #18 gives that figure open space while #19 surrounds its central form with overlapping figures and edge fragments.

Both works feature tooth-baring mouths built from tight black lines with white fill, though rawblocks #42 centers that motif on a flat yellow ground while #19 scatters it across a dense multi-figure composition.

lookingQuestion: The white rectangle near the upper center shares no visible connection to the figures around it—what does its placement do to how you move through the rest of the image?
ambiguities: The smaller forms at the lower edge are ambiguous—they read as crouching figures or as isolated body-part fragments; the line work does not resolve this.
QmNwgu79xP1QTzUwSkwawepFygmqNVk2zwNAA9p8pukBGr (nnotb #20) shares blue line work but its soft organic forms offer no strong formal parallel to #19's dense figure arrangement, so it was omitted.
